Input.doc: One client command for one tick. jump and dash are "pressed this tick" edges; the rest are held states.

seq.doc: Sequence number, 1-based, one per client sim tick.

yaw.doc: Look direction in radians. Yaw 0 faces -Z; positive yaw turns left.

pitch.doc: Look pitch in radians; positive looks up. Not used by movement.

ads.doc: Aiming down sights (held): slows ground movement.

skillQ.doc: First skill pressed this tick (the Trooper's grenade, the Assassin's grapple).

reel.doc: First skill button held: the Assassin's grapple reels in while it is (let go and you swing on the line as it is).

skillE.doc: Second skill pressed this tick (the Trooper's barrier, the Assassin's rolling dive).

ult.doc: Ultimate pressed this tick (the Trooper's bombardment, the Assassin's overdrive). Only the server acts on it.

hero.doc: One of HeroKinds: who the player is, which decides what the skill buttons do. The client sends what it believes; the server overwrites it with the truth before simulating.

overdrive.doc: The Assassin's overdrive is running. Like hero: the client sends what it believes, the server overwrites it.

slot.doc: Weapon slot pressed this tick: 0 none, 1 and 2 the hero's two guns (Trooper: rifle, sniper; Assassin: sniper, thunder spears), 3 hands (Trooper: fists; Assassin: blades).

runSpeedMult.doc: Run speed multiplier from the weapon in hand (empty hands run faster). Set by whoever simulates from their weapon state; the server recomputes it and ignores what a client sends.

adsSpeedMult.doc: Ground speed multiplier while aiming down sights, for the gun in hand (the sniper is much slower). The server recomputes it.

viewTick.doc: The server tick (fractional) at which this player's screen was showing other players, for lag compensation. 0 means the current tick (no rewind).

PlayerState.doc: Complete movement state. (x, y, z) is the centre of the player's feet. Metres and seconds, Y up.

crouching.doc: Crouched (hold the slide key without enough speed to slide).

dashCharges.doc: Fractional: regenerates continuously up to the maximum.

dashTime.doc: Seconds of dash remaining; 0 when not dashing.

airJumps.doc: Air jumps left; refilled whenever grounded.

wallRunning.doc: Running along a wall (airborne, gravity mostly off).

wallRunTime.doc: Seconds spent on the current wall run.

wallNormalX.doc: Direction pointing out of the last wall run on or jumped from (unit XZ), for the re-grab cooldown.

wallJumps.doc: Wall jumps used since last touching the ground.

wallCooldown.doc: Seconds before the wall in wallNormal can be grabbed or jumped off again.

rollT.doc: Seconds left of the Assassin's rolling dive (0 when not diving).

rollDirZ.doc: The unit direction of the dive.

grappling.doc: Being pulled to a grapple point (the Assassin's first skill).

grappleZ.doc: The point the grapple is hooked to.

grapple2.doc: A second hook is out as well: the pull is between the two (a V).

grapple2Z.doc: The point the second hook is on.

grappleLen.doc: How long the first hook's line is: it only gets shorter, and the player cannot go further from the hook than this (that is what makes the swing).

grapple2Len.doc: The same for the second hook.

grappleT.doc: Seconds since the last hook went out.

grappleStall.doc: Seconds the grapple has been reeling without getting closer (it lets go when this runs long: you are circling the hook).

slowT.doc: Seconds of slow left after a bullet hit (run speed is cut while above 0).

Entity.doc: What other players need to draw and interpolate someone. Every entity carries a teamId.

kind.doc: One of EntityKinds. Skill objects are entities too: a grenade in flight (flags 1: it is the marker that calls a bombardment, not a frag grenade), a barrier (yaw 0 spans X, a quarter turn spans Z), a bombardment (flags 1 once the shells are falling), a practice-range recharge pickup (sent only while it can be taken), the point a grappling player is hooked to (teamId is that player's id), a thunder spear (yaw and pitch are the way it points; flags 1 once its fuse is lit: stuck in a wall, or bounced off a body).

hero.doc: One of HeroKinds, for a player: which character to draw.

WeaponState.doc: Weapon fire-control state. Simulated identically on client and server from the inputs.

slot.doc: The weapon in hand: 0 rifle, 1 sniper, 2 empty hands.

gun.doc: Which gun `ammo` belongs to (0 rifle, 1 sniper): the last gun held, so empty hands keep it.

stash.doc: Rounds left in the other gun.

switchT.doc: Seconds until the weapon just switched to is ready; 0 when ready.

reloadT.doc: Seconds of reload remaining; 0 when not reloading.

cooldown.doc: Seconds until the next shot is allowed.

meleeT.doc: Seconds until a melee swing lands; 0 when not swinging.

meleeCooldown.doc: Seconds until the next melee is allowed.

skillQT.doc: Seconds until the first skill is ready again; 0 when ready.

skillET.doc: Seconds until the second skill is ready again; 0 when ready.

diveT.doc: Seconds until the Assassin's rolling dive dives (its wind-up: draw the blades); 0 when not winding up.

slashT.doc: Seconds until the Assassin's dash cut dashes (its wind-up: draw the blades and cut the X); 0 when not winding up.

PlayerHealth.doc: Health, shield and life state. Server-authoritative.

protectedFor.doc: Seconds of spawn protection left (ends early when you fire).

ult.doc: Ultimate charge, 0 to 1 (ready at 1). Fills over time and from damage dealt; kept through death.

hero.doc: One of HeroKinds: who you are playing this life.

overdrive.doc: Seconds of the Assassin's overdrive left; 0 when it is not running.

nextHero.doc: One of HeroKinds: who you will be on your next life (differs from hero after a change mid-life).

GameEvent.doc: Something that happened that a player should see. Resent in several snapshots; `seq` is per recipient so the client skips ones it has handled.

actor.doc: hit: you (the shooter); hurt: who shot you; kill: the killer.

other.doc: hit: who you hit; hurt: you; kill: the victim.

health.doc: hit and hurt: the victim's health after the hit (so the shooter can show a health bar).

shield.doc: hit and hurt: the victim's shield after the hit.

Shot.doc: A bullet that was fired, so every client can draw its tracer. Resent in several snapshots; `seq` is global to the room so the client skips ones it has handled. The bullet starts at the shooter's eye with this direction (spread already applied) and flies by the shared bullet physics.

tick.doc: Server tick the shot was fired.

gun.doc: Which gun fired the bullet to draw: 0 rifle, 1 sniper (a faster bullet).

MatchInfo.doc: Where the room is in its match cycle.

timeLeft.doc: Seconds left in this phase (countdown, live and results). 0 while waiting.

suddenDeath.doc: Time ran out with the lead tied: the next kill that makes a single leader ends the match.

winner.doc: Player id of the winner once ended; 0 for a draw or while playing.

minPlayers.doc: Players needed to start a match.

rematchVotes.doc: How many players have asked for a rematch while the results are showing.

Score.doc: One player's tally in the current match.

input.doc: The latest few inputs, oldest first. Resent redundantly so a lost message does not lose inputs; the server skips sequence numbers it already has.

t.doc: Client time in ms, echoed back in pong.

respawn.doc: Ask the server to put this player back at a spawn point.

rematch.doc: Vote to start another match while the results are showing.

hero.doc: Choose a hero. It takes effect on your next life, or at once in the practice range, outside a live match, while dead, or during spawn protection.

practice.doc: A practice-range helper (ignored in other modes): refill health and ammo, teleport back to the course start, or reset the targets.

level.doc: Level the server runs, for example greybox.

room.doc: Room code (the link that lets a friend join is ?room=<code>).

mode.doc: The room's mode: ffa or practice.

snapshot.doc: The world as this player may see it, 30 times a second.

ackSeq.doc: Last input sequence the server has simulated for you. `you` is your state right after it.

queued.doc: Inputs of yours still waiting on the server (a measure of how far ahead you are).

full.doc: Whether entities is a complete relevance baseline. False means it is a delta from the previous snapshot.

entities.doc: Changed entities, or every relevant entity when full is true (see entitiesFor).

removed.doc: Entity IDs removed from the previous relevance baseline.

events.doc: Recent events for you (hits you landed, hits you took, kills anyone made).

shots.doc: Recent shots fired by anyone (bullets to draw).

t.doc: The client time from the ping.

tick.doc: Server tick when the ping was handled.
